english.title: Person made bankrupt in Scotland / N. Ireland obtain credit in England and Wales
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person

(A)_[whose estate had been sequestrated in Scotland,]_
(B)_[who had been adjudged bankrupt in Northern Ireland,]_

before your discharge,

(C)_[obtained credit to the extent of **(..SPECIFY AMOUNT OF CREDIT OBTAINED..), being the prescribed amount or more, without giving the person from whom you obtained it the relevant information about your status]_
(D)_[engaged in a business under a name other than that in which your estate was sequestrated without disclosing to all persons with whom you entered into a business transaction the name in which that sequestration took place]_
(E)_[engaged in a business under a name other than that in which you were adjudged bankrupt without disclosing to all persons with whom you entered into a business transaction the name in which you were so adjudged]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 360(3) of, and schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
estate has been sequestrated in Scotland /
adjudged bankrupt in Northern Ireland before discharge did something in E / W
which would be an offence under s. 360(1)
if an undischarged bankrupt and the sequestration of estate /
adjudication in NI
were an adjudication under Part IX

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
